- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; adjust upward to reflect potential rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; apply downward correction to avoid overreaction.
- Model frequently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mixed; use 10–15 day moving average to smooth out noise.
- If sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from +0.67 to -0.33 within 3 days), model often fails to adjust; apply lagged correction by 2–3 days.
- When sentiment is consistently high but price is flat or declining, model may overfit recent trends; reduce forecast slope to reflect diminishing momentum.
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 5 days show strong upward momentum, model often overestimates; cap forecast at 1.5x recent high unless sentiment confirms continuation.
